description: Kansas’s earned income tax credit is claimed on the state income-tax return and is based on the federal EITC.
introduction: Kansas’s earned income tax credit is claimed on the state income-tax return and is based on the federal EITC.

sections.who: The 2025 Kansas instructions limit this credit to residents, excluding part-year residents and nonresidents. Federal EITC eligibility and the federal amount are needed first.
sections.get: For tax year 2025, Kansas calculates the credit at 17% of federal EITC. Follow the K-40 worksheet to apply the credit and its refundable portion.
sections.docs: Keep the federal EITC calculation, wage records and completed K-40 worksheet. Store dependent and residency evidence with your return.
sections.apply:
1. Use the tax booklet matching the year of the return. Calculate the federal credit before completing Kansas’s EITC worksheet.

  2. Enter the state credit and refundable amount as instructed on K-40. If the IRS has not yet calculated your federal EITC, the Kansas booklet explains filing without the credit and later amending.
sections.after: Keep copies of both returns. Respond to Revenue notices using the address or secure process in the notice.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: 2025 Kansas income-tax booklet.

Historical screenshots and background: USA Assistance. Screenshots may show an earlier application interface.

faqs: Can a part-year resident claim the 2025 Kansas credit?
The 2025 booklet says this credit is for residents only.
Is this a monthly assistance payment?
No. It is a state tax-return credit.
What if the IRS has not calculated my federal EITC yet?
Follow Kansas’s filing and amendment instructions; do not delay a required payment without checking them.
